facts.raw_span: a red tumor on her right upper arm that enlarged over 6 months
The lesion initially started as a small cutaneous nodule
no history of local trauma or insect bite
a 6 × 6-cm protuberant, thick-walled, and well-defined red bullalike tumor on the right upper arm
a nontender, firm-to-hard nodule was palpated
no regional lymphadenopathy
Hematologic, biochemical, and urinalysis tests were normal
multilocular spaces below the epidermis and a solid tumor present in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance
basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis and dilated lymphatic vessels in the dermis above the tumor

concepts.why: The presence of a well-defined red tumor with a hard nodule inside, multilocular spaces below the epidermis, and basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis are characteristic of pilomatrixoma.
The rapid growth of the tumor and its appearance as a protuberant, thick-walled, and well-defined red bullalike tumor are consistent with keratoacanthoma.
The presence of a firm-to-hard nodule and the tumor's appearance as a well-defined red bullalike tumor are consistent with dermatofibroma.
The presence of a well-defined red tumor with a hard nodule inside and multilocular spaces below the epidermis are consistent with epidermal inclusion cyst.
The presence of a firm-to-hard nodule and the tumor's appearance as a well-defined red bullalike tumor are consistent with lipoma.
The presence of a well-defined red tumor and dilated lymphatic vessels in the dermis above the tumor are consistent with hemangioma.
The presence of a firm-to-hard nodule and the tumor's appearance as a well-defined red bullalike tumor are consistent with neurofibroma.
The presence of a well-defined red tumor and the absence of regional lymphadenopathy are consistent with granuloma annulare.
